page: Amazon Web Services r7a.medium is an entry-level memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU clocked at 3.7 GHz. The compute resource is equipped with 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 4 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for vector instructions including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16. Memory capacity is 8.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. The instance does not include local storage or discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong single-threaded performance paired with overall throughput limitations stemming from the single-core topology. The instance achieves strong scores in single-core stress-ng tests (3029.48) and Geekbench single-core assessments (1946.0), placing it in the top quartile of tested instances. However, because multi-core metrics match single-core values, overall multi-threaded throughput ranks in the lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate uncached read rates of 33.86 GB/sec and write rates of 26.49 GB/sec. Redis SET throughput measures 2.65 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reaches 2.22 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, r7a.medium offers an accessible entry point to modern DDR5 memory and AMD Zen 4 architecture without the cost commitment of larger multi-core nodes. The primary operational tradeoff is total parallel compute capacity and the lack of bundled local NVMe storage, meaning disk I/O depends entirely on network-attached storage. The instance fits lightweight in-memory caching nodes, low-traffic relational databases, small data processing pipelines, and microservices requiring dedicated per-core RAM rather than aggregate CPU throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services r7a.medium is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. The configuration supplies 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU running at 3.7 GHz, supported by 8.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz. Hardware instruction sets include AVX-512 variants and cryptographic extensions. The instance features no local storage and zero GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core CPU execution, ranking in the top quartile for single-threaded processing in Geekbench and stress-ng. Conversely, multi-threaded capacity and memory bandwidth remain constrained by the single-core allotment. The r7a.medium provides resource efficiency for workloads demanding modern DDR5 memory density per core without multi-threaded CPU overhead, making it suitable for lightweight in-memory data stores, small relational databases, microservices, and modest background worker tasks.
